t: You're standing in Joseph Grimaldi Park, a public garden off Pentonville Road in Islington. This was once the burial ground of St James's Chapel, and the park is named after the clown Joseph Grimaldi, who is buried here. He was the most popular English entertainer of the Regency era, and he made the Clown the star of the pantomime, at Drury Lane, Sadler's Wells and Covent Garden. Clowns became known as Joey after him, and his catchphrase, Here we are again, is still heard in pantomimes.
